findings.message:
[P2] Restore nested permissions before removing a created tree

When a non-root candidate creates an out-of-scope directory tree and makes a nested directory non-writable, `_restoreDirectoryAccess` only adjusts the current path and its ancestors; the parent-first rollback then recursively removes the top directory while the nested directory is still inaccessible. This can raise `PermissionDenied`, leave the unauthorized tree behind, and surface an internal error instead of `write_scope`.

benchmarks/fixture.ts:412-419

[P2] Restore modes after granting access to allowed ancestors

When an allowed path is replaced by or creates a read-only directory containing an unauthorized child, this branch adds owner access so the child can be removed but never queues the ancestor's current mode in `directoryModes`. Because the allowed ancestor is not otherwise rolled back, it remains at the temporary writable mode, changing the command's allowed result and potentially affecting verification.

benchmarks/fixture.ts:463-465

summary: Permission recovery still fails for nested read-only trees and can leak temporary mode changes.

evidence: The new snapshot access grants cover the named unreadable-file and read-only-existing-directory cases, and `runVerification` now converts shell exceptions into failed verification outcomes before result and trajectory writing.

Rollback remains parent-first and does not grant access to nested directories before recursively removing a newly created unauthorized tree, so the permission-recovery and `write_scope` acceptance requirement is not fully met.
The added mode-grant branch also leaves a temporary mode on an allowed non-directory or newly created directory ancestor when removing an unauthorized descendant.
